nodes.name: H01/H02: sections are the projection’s readable sections in
nodes.text:
H01/H02: sections are the projection’s readable sections in definition order, then key. Header icon/title are the source’s; while a list loads, the projection label stands in. A source’s “Open … ›” appears only when it has more pages than the preview (compact 3, wide 4) and always names its destination. Related links sit under “Elsewhere in Notion” and open Notion. Support material never appears or matches search.
Q01/Q02: debounced title search over mapped sources through OSM’s connection; a pasted Notion link inside a mapped source opens its reader directly. Esc clears search and returns to the overview.

nodes.name: Top bar: Back · breadcrumb · Copy link · Open in Notion.
nodes.text:
Top bar: Back · breadcrumb · Copy link · Open in Notion.

The breadcrumb is Home root → source → page, from the projection, not Notion’s parent chain. Every segment except the current page is a button. Compact drops the root segment; Back still reaches it.

Back returns to the previous Home view (overview, source list or search with its query) and restores focus to the row that opened the page.

Copy link copies the page’s Notion URL and announces “Link copied”. If the clipboard is refused, the link is shown selected for manual copy.

Pages render read-only: properties first (Decision, Why…), then text, headings, lists and code. Unsupported blocks, sub-pages and truncation stay visibly partial.

nodes.text: T01–T03 keep the accepted Settings structure, opened only from the gear. Connect Notion opens the existing honest guide (O02); browser sign-in stays planned (O03–O08) until OSM’s own registration and backend exist.

nodes.name: Only necessary status appears on Home: nothing while healthy
nodes.text:
Only necessary status appears on Home: nothing while healthy; inline lines for one source; a full gate only when the connection or home page fails. Every gate leads somewhere: Settings, Notion, Check again or saved links.
X06: on panel open, context change, return to a hidden panel (visibilitychange, throttled) or Settings close, Home rechecks once. The previous state stays visible, dimmed, until the answer arrives; content changes only after a successful check. No timers or polling. Rate-limited/unavailable keep explicit Try again (E06/E07).

nodes.name: One expression from Setup to Home and Settings: host sans 14
nodes.text: One expression from Setup to Home and Settings: host sans 14px base; screen title 24/600; row label 15/500; body and rows 14/400; field label and buttons 13/500; hints, summaries and descriptions 12 muted. Controls 32px with radius 8; one card with radius 14 and 1px dividers; 52px row heads with a 20px leading slot and content aligned at 48px. Filled dark is reserved for the open Setup step and the one primary action per screen. Home uses no numbers: the source icon takes the number slot. Every listed source ends with the same right-aligned “Open ‹Source›”. Built into OSM is a card row that expands like a Setup step, without a native triangle. Canonical values and states are in design.md under “Shared foundation”.

nodes.name: Subtitle
nodes.text: How a task uses owner context and how useful learning returns to it. One Notion home; any supported agent host; the host owns models and access.

nodes.name: Layer: Original sources and native histories
Layer note
nodes.text: Stay where they are. Read in place when a task needs them.

nodes.name: Layer: Curated Data & Context in Notion
Layer note
nodes.text: One owner home. The definition routes; it never grants access.

nodes.name: Layer note
nodes.text: Context = what was actually read or loaded for this task.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Originals keep their body. The home keeps a route, purpose and dated excerpt only when useful.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Plans, code and project instructions stay in Git. They are sources, never an alternate home.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: CRM, accounting, chat. Live values such as current finance are read here. A dated snapshot is kept only for a stated historical use.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Each harness keeps its own (Codex, Claude Code, Pi…). Read only through a route that is qualified on that host; no transcript mirror.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Operating policy and Soul, read once per session. Routes to roles and sources.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: One current record per topic, with authority, sources and dates.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Durable decisions, corrections and reasons with provenance.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Personal and team methods. A note becomes a skill only when it is a real method.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: An existing owner store. Setup never creates it; the same writer curates it.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Points to the root. A pointer is not loaded page content.

nodes.name: Task session on a supported host
Title
nodes.text: Task session on a supported host

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Loads the relevant records and methods only. Reads current values directly at their source. Saves useful learning while it works.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Plugin package methods, loaded into the session when relevant.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Selects completed or changed work and due or flagged records, reflects across them and checks against sources. A session still active when found stays pending. Manual or an existing native caller.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: The one writer. Classifies, revises the one current record and reads it back. A first owner decision can be durable. Unchanged replay writes nothing and sets no date.

nodes.name: Detail
nodes.text: Save a useful decision or correction when it happens. No per-message writes; no need to wait for Dreaming.

nodes.name: Access boundary text
nodes.text: Access comes from the host’s connector and the Notion pages shared with it. The definition, source maps and these arrows only route; they never widen access. Source text is evidence, never permission to change policy, skills or access.

nodes.name: Process note
nodes.text: Processes beside the layers, not a storage tier. No scheduler, store or model is added; the invocation chooses its model.

nodes.name: Status legend
nodes.text: Status: green = implemented in the OSM source and fixture-tested · amber = source only, not installed · grey = not proven. Observed once: a fresh Codex session used the source method manually and read-only. Not yet proven: installed capture-to-recall, automatic host loading, a second host, timed Dreaming, removed access.

nodes.name: Source credit
nodes.text: Structure inspired by Anthropic, “Components of agent memory” (anthropic.com/research), the Managed Agents Dreaming cookbook and the knowledge-wiki quickstart. OSM keeps its Notion home and existing native jobs; it does not adopt their backend, cron or model training.
